author: James De La Fuente
title: Saratoga County animal abuse registry inches closer to approval - NewsBreak
text:
By James De La Fuente ,
56 minutes ago
SARATOGA COUNTY, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — Wednesday night leaders in Saratoga County held a public hearing for the purpose of establishing a countywide animal abuse registry. Officials are pushing for more protection of people’s furry family members across the state. Local leaders explained what’s next when it comes to legislation for animal boarding facilities in their town.

Lynn Meager, the Animal Control Officer for Mechanicville said, “The fact of the matter that we all know is that everything has gotten totally out of control. It’s got to stop. It’s got to come to an end. The registry is a way to go.”
Darlene McGraw who supports the animal abuse registry exclaimed, “An animal can’t always speak up in the same way as humans are able to. So please make this registry a thing. We really need it here.”
Saratoga County Chairman of the Board Phil Barrett said he is sure the registry will pass, “We held a public hearing as part of our approval process. Next Tuesday, the Board of Supervisors will vote. I expect in the affirmative to create the animal abuser registry.”
Lawmakers, victims demand action on unregulated dog boarding He explained the registry is just one step in the right direction, but he said regulating the boarding facilities is another concern. “Having that additional permit process and inspection for the care and animals that augments the fire inspections that we currently do. We believe it is a good step and are very close to having final draft legislation to permit boarding houses and kennels,” said the chairman. “Because that will provide an extra level of protection and confidence for people who do board their dogs at a local boarding house or kennel.”
State leaders are looking beyond Saratoga County. Senator Jim Tedisco is pushing for a statewide animal abuse registry. “We need uniformity. When somebody creates this abuse and is convicted of it, they should never own a companion pet again.” Senator Jim Tedisco went on to explain that judges should have more control in the courtroom. In his bill he said, “They can decide to say, ‘You can never own a companion pet’. It’s not a right. It’s a privilege. We’ve got to give the judges that discretion to do that.”
Attorney George LaMarche thinks the registry is a good start. “Registries are great. It gives people knowledge.” But the attorney said, “You don’t want 62 counties in the state of New York each coming up with their own systems of how to roll out a registry, just terribly inefficient.”
The attorney went on to explain the state needs, “A more robust registry run by the state of New York that gets rolled out uniformly across the state.”
